 Purdue parts ways with DC Kevin Kane
 Tom Dienhart @ TomDienhart1 47m 0 Share Share 
 Purdue has parted ways with defensive coordinator/linebackers coach Kevin Kane , the school announced today.
 The Boilermaker defense has struggled throughout the 2026 season, ranking among the worst in the Big Ten in all major categories. Following Saturday’s 34-29 homecoming loss to Maryland, Barry Odom felt it was time for a change.
 Purdue ranks 17th in the Big Ten in scoring defense (32.3 ppg); last in total defense (415.4 ypg); 17th in rush defense (170.8 ypg); 17th in pass defense (244.7 ypg).
 Purdue has allowed more plays of 20 or more yards (50), 30 or more yards (23) and 40 or more yards (16) than any Big Ten team. Only Rutgers (136) has allowed more plays of 10 or more yards than Purdue (124). And no Big Ten squad is more inept when it comes to stopping opponents on third downs than Purdue, which has seen foes convert 47.5 percent.
 Kane was hired from Minnesota to replace Mike Scherer as DC prior to the 2026 season. And the move surprised many. Kane had been DC from 2023-24 under Ryan Walters at Purdue. And the Boilermaker defenses struggled mightily back then.
 Kane’s second act in West Lafayette didn’t play well, either. Now, it’s over. 
 Kane signed a two-year contract at Purdue. He is being paid $850,000 in 2026 and will be owed $1 million for 2027.
 Now what? It is thought the staff is working through who will call the defense. It could be a collective defensive staff effort. Analyst Dave Steckel has DC experience. Stay tuned. Odom has his weekly press conference on Monday.
 Purdue (3-6 overall; 2-4 Big Ten) will play at Iowa (7-2; 4-2) on Saturday.
